Distributable cash rose to $15.5M from $12.7M
Cash available for dividends increased year over year; the company attributed the gain primarily to Mr. Lube + Tires adjusted EBITDA.
Net income fell to $5.5M from $8.7M
The decline contrasts with higher revenue and cash generation; impairment and higher expenses weighed on earnings.

The increase includes the acquired Mr. Lube + Tires business, so it is not a like-for-like growth comparison.
Payout ratio fell to 86.9% from 91.9%
A lower share of distributable cash was paid as dividends, providing more cash-flow coverage.
Sutton-related impairment was $4.7M
Weakness in the Canadian housing market reduced Sutton royalty payments and led to another impairment charge.
Mr. Lube + Tires Q3 system sales fell 1.7%
The acquired business faced weaker same-store sales, partially offset by sales from new locations.
